headline: Executives from the voice AI companies PolyAI and Otter said at the HumanX conference that voice AI has not yet had its ChatGPT moment, because answers still come too slowly and speech recognition still makes mistakes.
score_reason: Kept at 4: first reported by TechCrunch on 11 Oct 2026 and read in full, but it is opinion from the sellers of voice AI, made at a conference last month, with no new product or data.
importance_line: People who deal with automated phone lines and meeting transcripts are told by two industry insiders that voice assistants still respond too slowly and mishear key words, which they say costs trust, but these are opinions from executives whose companies sell voice AI and TechCrunch reports no new test or product.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Shawn Wen, chief technology officer of the enterprise voice AI company PolyAI, said at last month's HumanX conference that voice AI, despite models that can speak while listening, has not yet had its "ChatGPT moment" and that the next task is making machine reasoning fast enough for conversation to feel natural. Wen and Alex Gay, marketing chief of the meeting-notetaker company Otter, also said that speech recognition still misses key words and leaves the follow-up actions built on it flawed, and that people should be told when they are being recorded or are talking to an AI.
notes: Read TechCrunch in full. The remarks were made at the HumanX conference 'last month' (exact date not given), so QA may treat the event as older; TechCrunch is the first outlet to report them and no earlier edition of ours carried them. Executive opinion, no new data.
